items.title: Three Vanities Even a Trainee Must Still Overcome, Three Places Where Craving Takes Hold, and the Three Basic Sufferings

items.zh: 又有三種未究竟聖，共諸異生生死災患。若有於彼深厭怖者，當速斷除三種憍逸，修習現法涅槃方便。一、無病衰退，二、少年衰退，三、壽命衰退。其有智者，應觀未來如是三事定當隨逐。又有三種有情之類，貪瞋癡縛所依處所身分差別，能急繫縛諸有情類，閉在大苦生死牢獄。一、能饒益，二、能損害，三者、平等二種俱離。又有三處所生諸苦，遍攝有情所有眾苦。一、合會所生苦，二、乖離所生苦，三、平等相續苦。初由損害位和合故；第二由饒益位變壞故；第三於一切位相續而轉，麁重所攝，諸行所生，唯眾賢聖覺之為苦，非諸異生。
items.en: There are also three [calamities of] birth and death that noble ones not yet ultimate share with ordinary beings. One who is deeply weary and fearful of these should swiftly sever three kinds of vanity and cultivate the means to nirvāṇa in this very life. First, the decline of freedom from illness; second, the decline of youth; third, the decline of life itself. One who is wise should contemplate that these three things will, in the future, certainly follow. There are also three distinct bodily states, the bases on which the bonds of greed, hatred, and delusion depend, that tightly bind sentient beings and confine them in the great prison of suffering birth-and-death: first, what benefits; second, what harms; third, what is equally free of both. There are also three sources from which all suffering arises, comprehending the entirety of what sentient beings suffer: first, suffering born of union; second, suffering born of separation; third, suffering of even, continuous succession. The first is through the union of a harmful state; the second, through the ruin of a beneficial state; the third turns on continuously through every state, comprised of coarse weight, arisen from formations themselves — perceived as suffering only by the worthy and the noble, not by ordinary beings.

items.title: Three Kinds of Conceit That Block Stream-Entry, and the Three Seeds Spanning Past, Present, and Future

items.zh: 又有三種心高舉法，違害欲求沙門果證修方便者預流果支，能障沙門令不得證。一者、以己校量於他，謂我為勝，心生高舉；二者、以己校量於他，謂我相似，心生高舉；三者、以己挍量於他，謂我為劣，心生高舉。復有三種種子，當知能生一切諸行。一、已與果，二、未與果，三、果正現前。
items.en: There are also three ways the mind rises up in conceit, which injure the very supports of stream-entry for one who seeks and cultivates the means towards the fruits of the ascetic path, and obstruct that path's realisation: first, comparing oneself to another and thinking "I am superior," the mind rises up; second, comparing oneself to another and thinking "I am equal," the mind rises up; third, comparing oneself to another and thinking "I am inferior," the mind rises up. There are also three kinds of seed, which should be known to give rise to all conditioned formations: first, that which has already yielded its fruit; second, that which has not yet yielded its fruit; third, that whose fruit is presently manifesting.

items.title: The Three Times as the Basis of All Speech, and Matter Analysed Three Ways — Including the Rare Form Only Deep Meditation Can Perceive

items.zh: 又有三種諸行言說所依處。所謂去來今。又有三相，能攝一切色法自相。謂顯、形、作用，安立眼識所取之色。於自處所，障礙餘色行住，安立根色，若一切境界色；當知一切總有十色，及定地色。若得淨定，為引變化修方便者所有諸色，當知是內化心境界，亦是未滿變化心果。
items.en: There are also three bases on which speech concerning conditioned formations depends: namely, the past, future, and present. There are also three characteristics that comprehend the particular nature of all matter. [First, the visible:] colour, shape, and function, by which the matter grasped by eye-consciousness is established. [Second, the resistant:] whatever obstructs, in its own location, the movement and abiding of other matter establishes the matter of the faculties and the matter of every object; know that, altogether, there are ten [such] forms of matter. [Third,] there is matter belonging to the meditative realm. Matter possessed by one who, having attained pure concentration, cultivates the means to elicit transformation, should be known as the domain of an inwardly transforming mind, and also as the not-yet-complete fruit of a transforming mind.

items.title: Three Minds Still Trailed by Affliction, Three Grades of How Students Retain Teaching, and Three Doorways Into Seeing Impermanence

items.zh: 又有三種為諸煩惱所隨逐心。一、諸異生心，二、未滿學心，三、已滿學心。又有三種聽聞法者。一、於法於義不能受持；二、唯能領受，不能任持；三、能受能持。又有三法，是修行者觀身語意無常性觀趣入上首。一者、入出息，二者、尋伺，三者、想思。
items.en: There are also three minds still trailed by the afflictions: first, the minds of ordinary beings; second, the mind of the trainee not yet complete; third, the mind of the trainee just complete. There are also three kinds of one who hears the teaching: first, one who can retain neither the words nor their meaning; second, one who can only receive them, but cannot sustain them; third, one who can both receive and sustain them. There are also three phenomena that lead the practitioner's contemplation of the impermanent nature of body, speech, and mind: first, the in-and-out breath; second, applied and sustained thought; third, perception and intention.

items.zh: 又有三種尊勝應受敬養。一、年齒增上，二、族姓增上，三、功德增上。
items.en: Further, there are three kinds of eminence that should receive respect and offerings: first, eminence in age; second, eminence in family; third, eminence in good qualities.

items.title: Three Causes That Fix a Being's Destiny, How the Community Flags Wrongdoing in Good Faith, and Why a Buddha Alone Needs No Guarding

items.zh: 又有三種住定不定因。二是定因。一不定因。一、惡趣定因，謂無間業。二、善趣涅槃定因，謂無漏有為法。三、不定因，謂所餘法。又有三法，為令聖教得久住故，展轉舉罪。一者、現見身語現行違犯學處；二、從他聞；三、以餘相比度了知。又諸如來自說具足三不護德。為顯外道諸師內懷眾惡，自稱一切智者，實非一切智者。又欲令彼於如來所發起真實一切智信。
items.en: There are also three causes of fixed and unfixed destiny: two are causes of fixation, one is a cause of non-fixation. First, the cause fixing one to the evil destinies: the acts of immediate retribution. Second, the cause fixing one to a favourable destiny and nirvāṇa: the uncontaminated conditioned dharmas. Third, the cause of non-fixation: the remaining phenomena. There are also three things by which, so that the sacred teaching may long endure, wrongdoing is raised from one to another: first, directly witnessing bodily or verbal conduct that violates the precepts; second, hearing it from another; third, inferring it through other signs. The Tathāgatas themselves declare that they possess the three unguarded virtues in full. This is to show that the various non-Buddhist teachers, harbouring much evil within, falsely call themselves omniscient though they are not. And it is also to give rise, in those who hear it, to genuine faith in the Tathāgata's true omniscience.

items.title: The Three Fires That Burn the Mind, and the Three Genuine "Fires" Worth Honouring Instead

items.zh: 復有三種邪執所生大火所起有情燒惱。一、貪愛燒惱，二、愁憂燒惱，三、顛倒燒惱。又有三火，為化樂福邪事外火勝解有情，示無虛誑所應事火；雖實非火，假立火名。一者、父母，二者、妻子，三者、真實應供福田。
items.en: There are also three great fires, born of wrong grasping, by which sentient beings are burned and tormented: first, the burning torment of craving; second, the burning torment of grief; third, the burning torment of delusion. There are also three fires, taught in order to transform those beings who delight in merit but wrongly hold to tending an external fire, showing the genuine, non-deceptive objects that should be tended as fire: though not literally fire, the name "fire" is provisionally given to them. First, one's parents; second, one's spouse; third, the genuine field of merit worthy of offerings.

items.title: The Three Genuine Grounds of a Favourable Rebirth, and Pleasure Graded Across the Desire and Form Realms

items.zh: 又有三種，為諸樂欲增上生者、所說真實增上生道。一者、布施，得大財富；二者、持戒，得往善趣；三者、修定，遠離苦受，得生一向無有惱害樂世界中。又有三種諸受欲者劣、中、勝欲，觀待諸欲所生樂故。一、多用功力依緣諸欲，謂現前住所有諸欲。二、少用功力依心諸欲，謂樂化天所有諸欲。三、極少功力依心諸欲，謂他化天所有諸欲。又有三種超過諸欲劣、中、勝樂。一、有尋伺喜，二、無尋伺喜，三、離喜之樂。
items.en: There are also three genuine paths to a favourable rebirth, taught for those who delight in and wish for such a rebirth: first, giving, which yields great wealth; second, upholding precepts, which yields rebirth in a favourable destiny; third, cultivating concentration, which frees one from painful feeling and yields rebirth in a world of exclusively untroubled pleasure. There are also three grades — inferior, middling, and superior — of desire among those who enjoy the desires, relative to the pleasure those desires produce: first, desires depending on much exertion and external conditions, namely the desires possessed by those presently dwelling [among humans and in the lower heavens]; second, desires depending on the mind with little exertion, namely the desires possessed by the Heaven of Delighting in Transformation; third, desires depending on the mind with the least exertion, namely the desires possessed by the Heaven of Mastery over Others' Transformations. There are also three grades — inferior, middling, and superior — of pleasure that surpass the desires: first, joy accompanied by applied and sustained thought; second, joy free of applied and sustained thought; third, pleasure free even of joy.

blocks.text: More threes. Today includes the well-known "three fires" of greed, hatred, and delusion, paired with an unexpected list of three fires one *should* tend. Notice how the treatise takes a Brahmanical ritual image and gives it an ethical meaning.

A noble one not yet at the end of the path must overcome three **vanities** (憍逸): of health, youth, and long life. The three basic sufferings: of pain, of change, and of conditioned formations (Day 32). The last, the treatise says, is perceived "only by the worthy and noble". Venerable Miào Jìng: "worthy" (賢) means those at the inner-ordinary stage who feel it through practice.

Three conceits block stream-entry: "I am better", "I am equal", and "I am worse". How can the last be conceit? Venerable Miào Jìng: comparing myself, "I'm not as good, but inside I'm still not quite convinced." Any self-measurement is conceit (Day 15).

Matter is analysed as visible, resistant, and invisible-non-resistant (the last includes form produced in meditation, Day 21). Venerable Miào Jìng disagrees with the *Pīxún jì*'s reading of one passage as "only an analogy": he takes it as describing meditative matter itself.
Students retain teaching in three grades: dull, middling, and sharp. A teacher adjusts accordingly.

Faults are raised in the community "so that the teaching may endure". Master Cháng Bǎi gives the five qualities of one who raises them: gently, with kindness, at the right time, truthfully, and for benefit (Day 57). A Buddha alone needs no guarding, because he has no faults to conceal.

subs.head: Three fires, and three fires to tend

blocks.text: The **three fires** that burn the mind: greed, hatred, and delusion. Against them, three "fires" worth tending, borrowed from the Brahmanical household fires: one's **parents**, one's **wife** (Master Cháng Bǎi: the one who builds the household with you, to be cared for), and those **worthy of offerings** (renunciants). Venerable Miào Jìng on a phrase in this passage: it took him several readings to see that it means teaching those who delight in merit.
The move is characteristic of the Buddha's teaching: rather than condemning a ritual, he redefines it. The true sacred fires are the people one is bound to care for.
Giving, discipline, and meditation (Day 19), and pleasure graded across the desire and form realms.

quiz.q: The treatise says the suffering of formations is perceived "only by the worthy and noble." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say 賢 refers to, and how does the English render it?
options: 賢 is the inner-ordinary stage (the outer can also be called so), who feel it through practice; the English keeps only "noble ones"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: 賢 should be one who has reached the inner-ordinary stage — the outer can also be called worthy — but because they practise, they can feel this suffering. The English "noble ones" omits the worthy.

quiz.q: The third rising of conceit is thinking "I am inferior." How can that be conceit, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: comparing oneself one knows one is worse, yet inwardly one still isn't convinced — so it is still conceit
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Comparing myself with another, I'm not as good — but inside I'm still not quite convinced, so 'I am inferior' is still the mind rising up." Master Cháng Bǎi: the other is far better, but one thinks one is only slightly behind.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi, following the Pixunji, classify the three kinds of hearers?
options: persons of dull, middling, and sharp faculties
quiz.why: The *Pixunji*: "Know that this speaks of persons of dull, middling, and sharp faculties — the three kinds of hearers." Master Cháng Bǎi: the words are the expressing names and phrases; the meaning is what they express.

quiz.q: The treatise says faults are raised so that the teaching may endure. Which five qualities does Master Cháng Bǎi say raising a fault requires?
options: loudly, publicly, immediately, harshly, with heavy penalty
gently, with kindness, at the right time, truthfully, and for benefit
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "With five qualities — gentleness, a kind heart, timeliness, truthfulness, and benefit — faults are raised mutually." The three grounds are seeing, hearing, and suspicion. Venerable Miào Jìng: the Vinaya requires five conditions.

quiz.q: The second of the three fires to tend is 妻子, rendered "spouse and children." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain it?
options: as wife only — the one who builds a household with you, to be supported and served
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Second, 妻子 — the wife is the one who works together with you to build a family, also someone to be supported and served." Offering to the Three Jewels, filial care, and cherishing family are the true field of merit.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng read 為化樂福 in the passage on the three fires?
options: to be reborn in a happy land
after several readings he understood: it is to teach those who delight in merit
to make offerings to a fire god
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "When I first read this, 'to transform those who delight in merit,' it took several readings to understand: it means teaching those who delight in merit." The first fire, parents, is a fire of reverence.
